summary: For three days before a non-Jewish holiday for their idols, we may not do business with them. We don't want them to be happy and thank their idol on their holiday.

chunks.he: לִפְנֵי אֵידֵיהֶן שֶׁל גּוֹיִם שְׁלשָׁה יָמִים
chunks.en: For three days before the holidays of non-Jews,
chunks.st: On the three days before the festivals of gentiles
chunks.stMore: the following actions are prohibited, as they would bring joy to the gentile, who would subsequently give thanks to his object of idol worship on his festival:

words.note: Holidays they make for their idols.

chunks.en: it is forbidden to do business with them,
chunks.st: It is prohibited to engage in business with them;

words.note: Taking and giving means doing business.

chunks.en: to lend them things, or to borrow things from them,
chunks.st: to lend items to them or to borrow items from them;

chunks.en: to lend them money, or to borrow money from them,
chunks.st: to lend money to them or to borrow money from them;

chunks.en: to pay them what we owe, or to collect what they owe us.
chunks.st: and to repay debts owed to them or to collect repayment of debts from them.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: נִפְרָעִין מֵהֶן מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מֵצֵר לוֹ.
chunks.en: We may collect what they owe us, because paying back makes him sad.
chunks.st: One may collect repayment of debts from them because this causes the gentile distress.

chunks.en: The Rabbis said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to Rabbi Yehuda:

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמֵּצֵר הוּא עַכְשָׁיו,
chunks.en: Even though he is sad now,
chunks.st: Even though he is distressed now,

chunks.en: he is happy later on.
chunks.explain: He is glad the debt is gone, and may thank his idol.
chunks.st: when he repays the money, he is happy afterward
chunks.stMore: that he is relieved of the debt, and therefore there is concern that he will give thanks to his object of idol worship on his festival.

summary: Rabbi Yishmael says the days after their holidays are forbidden too. The Sages say only the days before are forbidden.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says:

chunks.he: שְׁלשָׁה יָמִים לִפְנֵיהֶם וּשְׁלשָׁה יָמִים לְאַחֲרֵיהֶם,
chunks.en: three days before their holidays and three days after them
chunks.st: On the three days before the festivals of gentiles and on the three days after them,

chunks.en: it is forbidden.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to engage in business with those gentiles.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: before their holidays it is forbidden,
chunks.st: It is prohibited to engage in business with them before their festivals,

chunks.en: after their holidays it is allowed.
chunks.st: but it is permitted to engage in business with them after their festivals.

summary: This mishnah lists the holidays of the non-Jews, like the king's birthday. Private celebrations of one person are forbidden only on that day and only with that man.

chunks.en: These are the holidays of the non-Jews:
chunks.st: And these are the festivals of gentiles:

chunks.en: Kalenda, and Saturnalia,
chunks.st: Kalenda, Saturnalia,

words.note: A Roman winter holiday.
Another Roman winter holiday.

chunks.en: and Kratesis, and the holiday of their kings,
chunks.st: and Kratesis, and the day of the festival of their kings,

words.note: A day honoring the king.

chunks.en: and the king's birthday,
chunks.st: and the birthday of the king,

chunks.en: and the day the king died.
chunks.st: and the anniversary of the day of the death of the king.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: Any death where they burn things in public,
chunks.st: Every death that includes public burning

chunks.en: has avodah zarah in it — it is a holiday for idols.
chunks.st: is a festival that includes idol worship,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: And one where they don't burn things,
chunks.st: and any death that does not include public burning

chunks.en: has no avodah zarah in it.
chunks.st: is not a festival that includes idol worship.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: The day a non-Jew shaves his beard and his long hair,
chunks.st: But in the case of the day of shaving his, i.e., a gentile’s, beard and his locks,

chunks.en: the day he came back from the sea,
chunks.st: and the day of his ascent from the sea,

chunks.en: and the day he came out of prison,
chunks.st: and the day that he left prison,

words.note: Prison.

chunks.en: and a non-Jew who made a feast for his son,
chunks.st: and also in the case of a gentile who prepared a wedding feast for his son

chunks.en: it is forbidden only on that
chunks.st: and celebrates on that day, engaging in business is prohibited only on that

chunks.en: day, and only with that man.
chunks.st: day and with that man.

summary: If a city is having an idol holiday, may we do business outside it, or travel there? It depends on the place and the road.

chunks.en: A city that has avodah zarah,
chunks.explain: It is having a holiday for its idol.
chunks.st: In the case of a city in which there is active idol worship,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: outside it, it is allowed to do business.
chunks.st: it is permitted to engage in business transactions with gentiles who live outside of the city.

chunks.en: If the avodah zarah was outside the city,
chunks.st: If the idol worship is outside the city,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: inside the city it is allowed.
chunks.st: it is permitted to engage in business within the city.

chunks.en: What about going there?
chunks.st: What is the halakha with regard to traveling there,
chunks.stMore: a place where a pagan festival is being celebrated?

chunks.en: When the road goes only to that place,
chunks.st: When the road is designated only for that place,

chunks.en: it is forbidden. But if he could walk
chunks.explain: People would think he is going to the idol's holiday.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to use the road,
chunks.stMore: as onlookers will assume that the traveler intends to join the festival.

chunks.en: on it to another place,
chunks.st: But if one were able to travel on it to arrive at another place,

chunks.he: מֻתָּר. עִיר שֶׁיֶּשׁ בָּהּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְהָיוּ
chunks.en: it is allowed. A city that has avodah zarah, and there were
chunks.st: it is permitted to use the road
chunks.stMore: to reach the place that is observing the festival.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: stores in it — some decorated, and some not decorated,
chunks.explain: Decorated stores paid money to the idol.
chunks.st: With regard to a city in which idol worship is practiced and in which there are stores that are adorned for the sake of idol worship and there are others that are not adorned,

chunks.en: this really happened in Beis She'an,
chunks.st: this was in fact an incident that occurred in Beit She’an,

words.note: Beis She'an is a city in Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.en: and the Sages said,
chunks.st: and the Sages said:

chunks.en: the decorated stores are forbidden, and the ones not decorated are allowed.
chunks.st: With regard to the adorned shops, it is prohibited to buy from them, but in the case of those that are not adorned it is permitted.

summary: Some things are used only for idol worship, so we may not sell them to non-Jews. Other things we may sell, unless the buyer says he wants them for his idol.

chunks.en: These things are forbidden to sell to non-Jews:
chunks.st: These are the items that it is prohibited to sell to a gentile
chunks.stMore: at any time of year, as they are used specifically for idol worship:

chunks.en: itzterubalin, and benos shuach and their stems,
chunks.st: Itzterubalin, benot shuaḥ, petotarot,

words.note: A kind of fruit.
Benos shuach are a kind of white figs.

chunks.en: and frankincense, and a white rooster.
chunks.st: frankincense, and a white rooster.

words.note: A sweet-smelling spice they burned for idols.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: it is allowed to sell him a white rooster
chunks.st: It is permitted to sell a white rooster

chunks.en: together with other roosters.
chunks.st: to a gentile provided that it is sold along with other types of roosters.

chunks.en: But when it is sold by itself,
chunks.st: But when it is sold by itself,

chunks.en: he cuts off its toe and sells it to him,
chunks.st: one should cut off its toe and sell it to the gentile,

chunks.he: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מַקְרִיבִין חָסֵר לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
chunks.en: because they don't bring a damaged animal to their idol.
chunks.st: because they do not sacrifice a defective animal to their object of idol worship.

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: And all other things,
chunks.st: And with regard to all remaining items,

chunks.en: if he says nothing, it is allowed,
chunks.st: without specification it is permitted to sell them,

chunks.en: but if he says they are for his idol, it is forbidden.
chunks.st: but with specification it is prohibited to sell them.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: even a good palm tree, and chatzav,
chunks.st: Even in the case of a good palm tree, ḥatzav,

words.note: A kind of plant.

chunks.en: and naklav, are forbidden to sell to non-Jews.
chunks.st: and naklav, it is prohibited to sell them to gentiles.

words.note: Another kind of plant.

summary: May we sell animals to non-Jews? Small animals depend on the local custom. Big animals that do work are never sold, so a Jew's animal won't work on Shabbos.

chunks.he: מְקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לִמְכֹּר בְּהֵמָה דַקָּה לְגוֹיִם,
chunks.en: In a place where people sold small animals to non-Jews,
chunks.st: In a place where the residents were accustomed to sell small domesticated animals to gentiles,

chunks.en: we may sell. In a place where they did not sell,
chunks.st: one may sell them. In a place where they were not accustomed to sell them,

chunks.en: we may not sell.
chunks.st: one may not sell them.

chunks.en: And in every place, we may not sell
chunks.st: But in every place, one may not sell

chunks.en: them big animals,
chunks.st: them large livestock,

chunks.en: calves or young horses,
chunks.st: calves, or foals,

chunks.en: whether whole or hurt.
chunks.explain: We don't want a Jew's animal to do work on Shabbos.
chunks.st: whether these animals are whole or damaged.
chunks.stMore: The Sages prohibited these sales lest a Jew’s animal perform labor for the gentile on Shabbat in violation of an explicit Torah prohibition, as explained in the Gemara.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah allows a hurt animal.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda permits the sale of a damaged animal
chunks.stMore: because it is incapable of performing labor,

chunks.en: And Ben Beseira allows a horse.
chunks.st: and ben Beteira permits the sale of a horse
chunks.stMore: for riding, because riding a horse on Shabbat is not prohibited by Torah law.

summary: We may not sell non-Jews dangerous animals, or help them build places used to hurt people. We may help build a bathhouse, but not the spot where they put an idol.

chunks.he: אֵין מוֹכְרִין לָהֶם דֻּבִּין וַאֲרָיוֹת וְכָל
chunks.en: We may not sell them bears, or lions, or any
chunks.st: One may not sell bears, or lions, or any item

chunks.en: thing that can hurt many people.
chunks.st: that can cause injury to the public, to gentiles.

chunks.en: We may not build with them a basilica,
chunks.st: One may not build with them a basilica [basileki],

words.note: A big building where judges sat.

chunks.en: a courthouse, or a stadium,
chunks.st: a tribunal [gardom], a stadium [itztadeyya],

words.note: Where they judged people to be killed.
A big field where people were hurt for a show.

chunks.he: וּבִימָה. אֲבָל בּוֹנִים עִמָּהֶם בִּימוֹסְיָאוֹת וּבֵית מֶרְחֲצָאוֹת.
chunks.en: or a tall platform. But we may build with them small platforms and bathhouses.
chunks.st: or a platform. But one may build with them small platforms [bimmusiot] and bathhouses.

chunks.he: הִגִּיעוּ לַכִּפָּה שֶׁמַּעֲמִידִין בָּהּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
chunks.en: Once they reach the dome where they put up their avodah zarah,
chunks.st: Even in this case, once he reaches the arched chamber in the bath where the gentiles put up objects of idol worship,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: it is forbidden to build.
chunks.st: it is prohibited to build it.

summary: We may not make jewelry for idols. We may not sell non-Jews things attached to the ground in Eretz Yisrael. Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei argue about renting and selling houses and fields in different places.

chunks.en: We may not make jewelry for avodah zarah,
chunks.st: And one may not fashion jewelry for an object of idol worship,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: like necklaces, nose rings and rings.
chunks.st: and this applies to jewelry such as necklaces [katla’ot], nose rings, and rings.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: if it is for pay, it is allowed.
chunks.st: If one fashions them in exchange for payment, it is permitted.
chunks.stMore: The mishna returns to the issue of selling items to gentiles:

chunks.en: We may not sell them something attached to the ground,
chunks.st: One may not sell to a gentile any item that is attached to the ground,

chunks.en: but he may sell it once it is cut off.
chunks.st: but one may sell such an item once it is severed from the ground.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: מוֹכֵר הוּא לוֹ עַל מְנָת לָקוֹץ.
chunks.en: he may sell it to him if it will be cut off.
chunks.st: It is not necessary to sever the item from the ground; rather, one may sell it on the condition that it be severed.

chunks.he: אֵין מַשְׂכִּירִין לָהֶם בָּתִּים בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: We may not rent houses to them in Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: One may not rent a house to a gentile in Eretz Yisrael,

chunks.en: and of course not fields.
chunks.st: and needless to say one may not rent fields to them, as explained in the Gemara.

chunks.en: And in Syria we may rent houses to them,
chunks.st: And in Syria one may rent houses to gentiles,

words.note: A land next to Eretz Yisrael.

chunks.en: but not fields.
chunks.st: but one may not rent fields.

chunks.en: And outside Eretz Yisrael we may sell them
chunks.st: And outside of Eretz Yisrael

chunks.en: houses and rent them fields,
chunks.st: one may sell houses and rent fields to gentiles;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: in Eretz Yisrael we may rent houses to them,
chunks.st: In Eretz Yisrael one may rent houses to gentiles

chunks.en: but not fields.
chunks.st: but one may not rent fields.

chunks.en: And in Syria we may sell houses and rent fields.
chunks.st: And in Syria one may sell houses to them and rent fields,

chunks.en: And outside Eretz Yisrael we may sell both.
chunks.st: and outside of Eretz Yisrael one may sell both these, houses, and those, fields.

summary: Even where renting a house is allowed, it may not be rented for living in, because he will bring his idols into it. And a bathhouse may never be rented to a non-Jew.

chunks.en: Even in a place where they said we may rent,
chunks.st: Even in a place with regard to which the Sages said that it is permitted for a Jew to rent a house to a gentile,

chunks.en: they did not mean for a house to live in,
chunks.st: they did not say that one may rent it for use as a residence,

chunks.he: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מַכְנִיס לְתוֹכוֹ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
chunks.en: because he will bring avodah zarah into it,
chunks.st: because the gentile will bring objects of idol worship into it,

words.note: Avodah zarah, "strange worship", means worshipping idols.

chunks.en: as it says in the Torah: "And do not
chunks.st: as it is stated:

words.note: The fifth book of the Torah.

chunks.en: bring an abomination into your house."
chunks.st: “You shall not bring an abomination into your house” (Deuteronomy 7:26),
chunks.stMore: and this is still considered the house of a Jew.

words.note: Something Hashem hates, like an idol.

chunks.en: And in every place he may not rent
chunks.st: And for the same reason, in every place,

chunks.en: him the bathhouse,
chunks.st: one may not rent a bathhouse to a gentile,

chunks.en: because it is called by his name.
chunks.explain: People will think the Jew runs it on Shabbos.
chunks.st: since it is called by the name of the owner,
chunks.stMore: and onlookers will think that the Jew is operating it on Shabbat.
